rounds.title: BOHEMIA UIBOOK, ROUND 01: FINAL FANTASY X (Square, 2001)
BOHEMIA UIBOOK , ROUND 02: MACHINE PARTY / MIKE KLUBNIKA (2026)

_meta.what: Machine-readable index over the BOHEMIA UIBOOK: every game studied for its interface, one round per file. Every citable id resolves to a real finding with a lens and a port verdict. Generated by tools/bohemia_uibook_index.py; never hand-edited.
_meta.why: THE UI STUDY LAW (8/26/26). A study whose findings cannot be cited is an essay, and an essay changes nothing. This is the questbook machine pointed at interfaces.

FFX.D01.because: Bohemia is 120 BPM and EVERYTHING QUANTIZES TO THE BEAT. We want FFX's readable list while running something closer to ATB's clock. That is a real tension and pretending it is not is how a study becomes a fan page. WHAT THIS LANE THINKS, ROUTED, NOT DECIDED: the beat should be the METRONOME, not the shot clock. I-MOVE-YOU-MOVE already says the world advances when you act. If standing still costs nothing, the player has all the time in the world to read the list, and the beat only decides WHEN the action lands, not how long you get to think. That keeps both. It is COMBAT's and RUN's call, not mine.
FFX.D01.port: REFUSE, AND THIS IS THE HARDEST THING IN THE ROUND
FFX.D01.title: NO CLOCK MEANS NO PANIC, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE LIST READABLE
FFX.D01.what: CTB replaced the series' Active Time Battle. The world PAUSES on your turn and you have an indefinite period of time to choose.
FFX.D01.why: This is the finding under the finding. FFX's famous turn preview only works because there is time to read it. A preview you have no time to read is decoration. Square did not add a preview to ATB; they removed the timer FIRST.

FFX.D02.because: UI-2 says THE ACTION BUTTON DOES ACTIONS AND NEVER CHANGES MEANING. A verb-then-target with a visible way out is exactly the shape that keeps that promise: the button always means "do the thing I have picked", and picking is reversible until the moment it is not.
FFX.D02.title: TARGETING IS A SENTENCE, AND YOU CAN STOP HALFWAY
FFX.D02.what: Choose a verb, and only then the valid targets light up and an arrow bobs over the current one. Circle commits, Triangle backs out, at every step.
FFX.D02.why: The mistake is caught before it costs anything. Two steps and a cancel is the cheapest error-prevention there is, and it is why nobody has ever rage-quit FFX for hitting the wrong thing.

FFX.D03.because: THERE ARE NO RUNS and there is no party, so the letter of it cannot come. The shape lands on the experience tree: the 60 mini bosses each hand you a new way to interact with Bohemia, and a hundred-hour kit needs a way to change what is ready WITHOUT a loadout screen. FFX's answer is the one to copy, the change is free, but only on the beat you were about to spend anyway, and only to the slot you were about to spend it on. No pause menu, no cost, no abuse.
FFX.D03.title: THE SWAP IS FREE, BUT IT IS SCOPED
FFX.D03.what: On a character's turn you can swap them out for anyone on the bench with one button, at no cost in turns. But ONLY the character whose turn it is can be swapped. You cannot stand there cycling the whole roster for free.
FFX.D03.why: A generous affordance with one honest limit. It puts the entire seven-person cast into every fight without a party-management screen and without letting the player abuse it.

FFX.D04.because: THE LAW SAYS IT IN OUR OWN WORDS, "a real kit of abilities recharged by VERBS, not timers" (8/26, THERE ARE NO RUNS). His favourite game shipped that exact idea in 2001 and we did not notice it was already solved. Overdrive Modes are the closest thing in any Final Fantasy to the rule we wrote down this week.
FFX.D04.title: THE BIG VERB IS EARNED BY A VERB YOU CHOOSE
FFX.D04.what: Overdrive is a per-character gauge sitting next to their HP that fills from what HAPPENS, then unlocks one big move. And Overdrive MODES let the player choose WHICH event charges it, taking damage, an ally taking damage, healing, and so on. You pick what your power is made of.
FFX.D04.why: The gauge is not a timer. It is a record of how you have been playing.

FFX.L01.because: Bohemia's fork 5 (THE DIRT) is the same idea in a different material. FFX's interface is made of glass; ours would be made of a dirty steel plate. Both say the same thing: the interface is a thing, not a page.
FFX.L01.caution: DO NOT COPY THE TRANSLUCENCY. FFX gets away with glass because its battle backgrounds are low-contrast and softly lit. Bohemia's world is high-contrast pixel art at 1:1, and text over it at 40% opacity is unreadable. Opaque plate, grime on the plate, world visible AROUND it, never THROUGH it.
FFX.L01.title: THE MENU IS A PANE OF GLASS LAID ON THE WORLD
FFX.L01.what: Every FFX panel is a translucent deep-indigo box with a thin light border and a soft inner gradient, drawn over the live scene. The world keeps moving behind it. The menu never replaces the picture, it is laid on top of it.
FFX.L01.why: The interface reads as an OBJECT with a material, not as a document. And because the world stays visible, opening a menu never feels like leaving.

FFX.L02.because: MEASURED 8/26: BOHEMIA HAS NO TYPEFACE. The alpha asks for one called Space Grotesk in exactly one place, never loads it, and has no font file. Every letter in the build is whatever the phone decided. That is what makes fork 4 on the UI page a real decision and not a cosmetic one.
FFX.L02.title: ONE FACE, AND IT WAS CARRYING MORE THAN ANYONE KNEW
FFX.L02.what: One typeface across the entire game, in one weight, at essentially two sizes. The 2013 HD Remaster changed that typeface and the menu cursor and almost nothing else material. Ten years later players still say the remaster damaged the game, and the type is the thing they name.
FFX.L02.why: A typeface is not decoration in a game with this much reading. It is the voice the game speaks in. Swap it and the same words sound like someone else.

FFX.L03.because: This answers fork 3 from inside his own favourite game. Bohemia's world is desert tan and GOLD LIGHT, and LIGHT = TERRITORY is law: gold means a lamp is on and somebody owns that ground. If the buttons are gold too, gold stops meaning light. The UI has to live where the world does not, which is the argument for BONE.
FFX.L03.title: THE INTERFACE LIVES IN A HUE THE WORLD DOES NOT USE
FFX.L03.what: Spira is tropical, turquoise water, wet sand, green, warm skin. The menus are deep indigo, a value and a hue the world barely touches. The interface and the world are never competing for the same part of the eye.
FFX.L03.why: Separation by HUE costs nothing and works before you read a single word.

FFX.L04.because: NO DAMAGE BEFORE THE DIAL is our own law and it is not negotiable. The SHAPE is banked for the day the dial exists; the content waits. Recording it here so nobody has to rediscover it, and so nobody ships it early.
FFX.L04.lens: signs and feedback (Hodent) · meta UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon)
FFX.L04.title: THE NUMBERS ARE BIG AND THEY FLY
FFX.L04.what: Damage pops off the target in a large face, arcs upward, and fades. 9999 is a landmark players chase for a hundred hours.
FFX.L04.why: The feedback is bigger than the event. That is deliberate: a hit you can barely see reads as a hit that barely happened.

FFX.L05.because: Playtest dispatch item 7 is "THE GAME KINDA RUNS LIKE SHIT", measured at 24.2 seconds to first play on throttled 4G. Some of that is real load and needs real optimisation, which is RUN's. But some of the FEELING is that our panels appear rather than arrive. That half is this lane's and it is cheap.
FFX.L05.caution: motion has a budget on a phone and this lane does not get to spend RUN's frame time. Transform and opacity only, never layout.
FFX.L05.screen: battle entry, menu open, cutscene handoff
FFX.L05.title: THE INTERFACE MOVES IN AND OUT INSTEAD OF CUTTING
FFX.L05.what: FFX slides its panels in and out. It very rarely hard-cuts from one screen state to another, and on a 2001 console it holds that even across the cutscene-to-battle handoff.
FFX.L05.why: A transition that MOVES reads as faster than a cut that waits, even when the clock says otherwise. Motion tells you the machine is alive.

FFX.R01.because: Bohemia is I-MOVE-YOU-MOVE on a 120 BPM clock, and combat is "Rogue Fable 4 with 120 BPM everything". The beat is the clock the turns run on. Right now that clock is a FELT thing with no picture: the player hears it and never sees who the next few beats belong to. FFX has the exact answer, shipped in 2001, and we already have the data to fill it.
FFX.R01.caution: FFX's list is a tall column on the right of a 4:3 screen. On an iPhone in portrait the right edge is where the thumb lives (SHARED -5). Ours has to run along the TOP, or be short enough not to reach into the thumb.
FFX.R01.port: TAKE, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS ROUND FOUND.
FFX.R01.title: THE FUTURE IS ON SCREEN
FFX.R01.what: The CTB window is a stack of portraits along the upper right showing WHO ACTS NEXT, in order, several turns ahead. It is not a bar you interpret. It is a LIST you read.
FFX.R01.why: FFX runs a hidden simulation, agility, action rank, tick counters. Instead of teaching the player that arithmetic, it does the arithmetic and shows THE ANSWER. The player never computes anything and still plans four moves out.

FFX.R02.because: Every Bohemia ability that costs beats should show its cost as a change in the beat list BEFORE the player commits, not as a number in a tooltip and not as a surprise afterwards. This is also how the 60 mini-boss abilities get taught without sixty tutorials.
FFX.R02.title: THE PREVIEW IS THE TUTORIAL
FFX.R02.what: The turn list RE-SORTS LIVE while you are still choosing. Move the cursor onto a slow, heavy ability and watch your own portrait slide further down. Hover Slow and watch the enemy's icons fall.
FFX.R02.why: The rule "weaker abilities cost less cooldown" is never written down anywhere. It is DEMONSTRATED, for free, every time the player compares two commands. The system teaches itself by being visible.

FFX.R03.because: THERE ARE NO RUNS and there is ONE character for a hundred hours, so a menu cannot tell people apart here, there is only him. But the same law says 60 MINI BOSSES each hand you A NEW WAY TO INTERACT WITH BOHEMIA. So the action list IS the experience tree made visible: what you can do is what you have beaten. The menu stops being a control panel and becomes a trophy case, and it grows for a hundred hours.
FFX.R03.title: THE COMMAND LIST IS THE CHARACTER SHEET
FFX.R03.what: Every character's command menu is DIFFERENT. Rikku has Steal and Use. Auron has Break. Kimahri has Lancet. You learn who somebody is by reading what their menu offers, before you ever read a stat.
FFX.R03.why: The menu is not a list of buttons, it is a portrait. Identity is expressed in what a person is ALLOWED to do.

FFX.R04.because: Cheap, invisible, and the demo will have people opening the phone and the action list hundreds of times in twenty minutes.
FFX.R04.title: THE MENU REMEMBERS WHERE YOU WERE
FFX.R04.what: The cursor returns to the last thing you chose. Attack stays under the cursor. The item you used last time is where you left it.
FFX.R04.why: In a game with thousands of menu openings, one saved keypress each is a measurable amount of a player's life. Nobody ever notices this working. Every player notices it missing.

FFX.R05.because: Directly serves NO ESSENTIAL INFORMATION BY COLOUR ALONE and its sister rule for sound: if the consequence is written at the point of decision, the player never has to have heard or seen a cue they missed.
FFX.R05.lens: clarity (Hodent) · Pinelle/Wong/Stach (heuristics mined from what players actually complained about across 108 games)
FFX.R05.title: THE READOUT SAYS WHAT IT DOES, NOT WHAT IT IS
FFX.R05.what: Selecting a target names it and shows the consequence in the same breath, the enemy's name, and whether this will help or hurt. The information appears at the moment of the decision, not in a screen you have to go find.
FFX.R05.why: Information delivered late is information the player has to REMEMBER, and memory is the most expensive thing a UI can spend.

FFX.W01.because: Bohemia already puts SLEEP (8 HOURS, SAVES) on the action button. Making the save a PLACE instead of a menu row is more Bohemia than any menu will ever be, and it wires straight into two other rulings: DANGER BY PLACE (Valheim-style district tiers) and LIGHT = TERRITORY. A place you can save is a place somebody is keeping the lights on. The safe map and the light map become the same map.
FFX.W01.lens: diegetic UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon: inside the fiction AND inside the geometry) · signs and feedback (Hodent)
FFX.W01.title: THE SAVE POINT IS A THING YOU WALK TO
FFX.W01.what: A Save Sphere is a glowing object standing in the world. You walk to it and touch it. It saves, it heals, and its presence is a warning: something is about to happen, this is the last quiet place.
FFX.W01.why: One object doing four jobs, a save, a heal, a landmark, and a held breath, and it costs zero screen space because it IS the screen.

FFX.W02.because: THEY SPEAK SPANGLISH (8/25, LOCKED) and that law has a hard rule inside it: LANGUAGE NEVER GATES REQUIRED INFORMATION. FFX's version DOES gate information behind language, that is the whole mechanic. So we cannot take it as built. HIS OWN LAW AND HIS FAVOURITE GAME DISAGREE HERE, and naming that is the job. What ports is the shape applied to things that are NOT required: the graffiti, the faction tags, the radio, the parts of the valley that are atmosphere. Never a quest step, never a name, never a direction.
FFX.W02.lens: meta UI (Fagerholt & Lorentzon) · the fiction axis
FFX.W02.port: ADAPT, AND THERE IS A HARD LIMIT
FFX.W02.title: THE INTERFACE TEACHES YOU A LANGUAGE, ONE LETTER AT A TIME
FFX.W02.what: Al Bhed characters speak in what looks like gibberish. Scattered across the world are Al Bhed Primers, and each one you find permanently decodes ONE LETTER, everywhere, retroactively, for the rest of the game. Your interface literally becomes more legible the longer you play.
FFX.W02.why: Comprehension as progression. Nothing else in the medium does this. It makes a hundred-hour game reward attention with UNDERSTANDING rather than with stats.

FFX.W03.because: Bohemia is an open valley of 27+ districts and he has already reported being "launched into a random part of the city" and walking through it lost. A clean empty screen is not a style you choose, IT IS SOMETHING A CORRIDOR PAYS FOR. If we copy the empty screen without the corridor we get a beautiful HUD over a player who has no idea where he is. We have to EARN the empty screen with landmarks and light, not declare it. Anyone who quotes "FFX has no HUD" at this project without quoting this paragraph is quoting half a finding.
FFX.W03.port: REFUSE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT CUTS AGAINST US HARDEST
FFX.W03.title: THERE IS ALMOST NO HUD, BECAUSE THERE IS ALMOST NO DECISION
FFX.W03.what: Walking around Spira there is essentially nothing on screen. No minimap, no compass, no health bar, no quest marker. FFX is famous for it.
FFX.W03.why: It can afford that because FFX is a CORRIDOR. There is no world map for most of the game. The level does the navigating, so the interface does not have to.

FFX.W04.because: WE HAVE NO VOICE ACTING AND WILL NOT HAVE ANY. Every ounce of the performance in Bohemia is carried by the words and by a 112px pixel face. So our dialogue sheet must be the OPPOSITE of FFX's: bigger, with the speaker's face IN it, with room for the line to breathe, which is what the run already does. Copying FFX's thin band here would be copying the consequence of a budget we do not have. The current sheet is right and this study says so.
FFX.W04.title: THE TEXT BOX IS THIN BECAUSE THE PERFORMANCE IS THE CONTENT
FFX.W04.what: FFX was the first Final Fantasy with voice acting. The characters are on screen, lit and acting, and the subtitle is a thin band at the bottom that gets out of the way.
FFX.W04.why: The box is small because the box is not carrying the scene. The actors are.

MP.D01.because: There is no "in front of you" in a three-quarter top-down game on a phone. The camera looks DOWN at a character; it never looks AT an object at arm's length, so a diegetic terminal has nowhere to be. Anyone who reads "Final Fantasy 10 meets Machine Party" and starts drawing a first-person control panel has copied the thing that cannot come and skipped the four that can. What survives the port is one sentence of it, and it is MP.D02 and MP.D03 below.
MP.D01.port: REFUSE, IN THE LETTER. THIS IS THE ONE PEOPLE WILL TRY TO COPY AND CANNOT.
MP.D01.title: THE MACHINE IS THE INTERFACE
MP.D01.what: Across his whole catalogue the interface is the thing in front of you: terminals, keys, switches, panels. s.p.l.i.t is "raw keyboard-driven interactions, terminal-based puzzles". The tension comes from OPERATING A MACHINE, not from reading a HUD laid over one.
MP.D01.why: A machine has weight, sequence and consequence. A menu has none of those; it has options. Operating something is dramatic in a way choosing something is not.

MP.D02.because: Post-economic-apocalypse Las Vegas is full of machinery that outlived the people it was for, which is the same sentence from the other end. Hold every object in the valley against it: was this shaped for a hand, or shaped for a job? A parking meter, a fare box, a slot machine and a fuel pump all answer the second way, and all four are already in the districts. It is a test the world lane can run today without cooking anything.
MP.D02.lens: form follows function (Hodent), inverted on purpose
MP.D02.title: DESIGNED FOR A PURPOSE, WITH NO THOUGHT FOR THE USER
MP.D02.what: On the machines in Buckshot Roulette: everything is built to do one specific job and nothing about it was shaped for a human hand.
MP.D02.why: It is a rule you can hold an object against and get a straight yes or no, which almost no aesthetic note manages. It is also the whole difference between industrial-LOOKING and industrial.

MP.D03.because: Final Fantasy 10 already gave us the phone-sized version of this in FFX.D02: pick the verb, THEN pick the target, and back out at any point. That is operating in two stages with a way to stop, on a touchscreen, and the action button never changes what it means (UI-2). Klubnika's version is why that shape is worth keeping rather than collapsing into one tap for speed.
MP.D03.lens: user control and flexibility (Hodent) - error prevention (Hodent)
MP.D03.title: YOU OPERATE IT, YOU DO NOT COMMAND IT
MP.D03.what: You do not select "shoot dealer" off a list. You pick the gun up, you point it, and you pull. The verb is carried out with your hands in stages, and each stage is a place you could still stop.
MP.D03.why: Stages make the decision feel like yours. A one-tap command from a menu is over before it is felt.

MP.L01.because: He killed all three dirt options on the UI page on 8/27, and that is not a contradiction of this finding, it is a correction of where I aimed it. Klubnika's grime unifies THE ROOM YOU ARE STANDING IN. I took a world technique and put it on a menu, which is the one surface in the game that is NOT part of the room. The interface is not another object in the scene, it is the sheet of instructions laid over the scene, and dirtying it makes it look like a texture that failed rather than a thing that has been used. THE FINDING IS GOOD AND IT BELONGS TO THE WORLD LANE, WHERE THE GRIME SHEET IS ALREADY WIRED AT HIS RULED 0.30. It does not belong on his buttons and he was right to say so.
MP.L01.lens: consistency (Hodent) - the mechanism behind "it reads as one room"
MP.L01.port: REFUSE, FOR THE INTERFACE. IT IS THE WORLD'S, AND IT ALWAYS WAS.
MP.L01.title: THE GRIME CROSSES THE SEAM, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS ONE PLACE
MP.L01.what: Klubnika on texturing: he "added dirty and grimy leaks to every corner, which blends everything together rather than having different objects." One filth pass laid over everything, indifferent to where one object stops and the next begins.
MP.L01.why: A wall, a floor and a machine that share a stain are one building. Three surfaces each perfectly textured that share nothing are three assets. The dirt, not the palette, is what makes a room read as a place.

MP.L02.because: This is the fork he answered on 8/27. He said yes to the HEAVY line, 2px at 3.78 to 1 against the panel, and no to the hairline that measured 1.22. His vote and Klubnika's steel are the same instinct, and the number now says so.
MP.L02.port: TAKE, AND HE ALREADY TOOK IT
MP.L02.screen: the table, the gun, the terminal
MP.L02.title: EVERYTHING IS THICK
MP.L02.what: The interface objects are deliberately CHUNKY. Heavy metal shapes, thick edges, industrial smoke, club light reflecting off the gun. Nothing in his work is a hairline.
MP.L02.why: A thick thing reads at a glance and reads in bad light. It also reads as MADE, out of steel, by somebody who was not thinking about elegance.

MP.L03.because: Bohemia is 44px three-quarter pixel art on a phone and a photograph pasted into that is mush. But the finding explains something already measured here: his bought tile library reads edge 18.4 and grain 61% where painted art reads 9.4 and 26%, and the reason is that photographs ARE uncorrelated at the pixel. HIM LOVING THIS LOOK AND HIM BUYING THAT LIBRARY ARE THE SAME TASTE POINTING AT THE SAME PHYSICAL PROPERTY. The technique cannot come. The measurement it explains is already in the world lane's hands.
MP.L03.title: THE TEXTURES ARE PHOTOGRAPHS OF REAL THINGS
MP.L03.what: He photographs his own textures, mainly of electronics, and urban-explores abandoned factories for reference. The Volta electrical component facility in Tallinn, which he went back to "a dozen times".
MP.L03.why: Photographic surfaces are uncorrelated at the finest scale, which is a thing you can measure. It is why his rooms feel like rooms instead of like materials.

MP.L04.because: Bohemia's world is desert tan and gold light, and LIGHT = TERRITORY says the gold means somebody is keeping a lamp on. So our material list is already written: sun-bleached tan, dead concrete, and the gold of the few lights left. What ports is the discipline, not the colours: the interface may only use what the valley is made of, plus the one cold that the valley does NOT have, which is what he chose on 8/27 for exactly this reason.
MP.L04.title: THE ROOM IS MADE OF THREE MATERIALS AND NO MORE
MP.L04.what: Concrete, steel, and a sick electric light. His environments are brutalist and the palette is what the building is physically made of, not a colour scheme chosen on top of it.
MP.L04.why: When the palette IS the material list, nothing on screen can be off-model, because every colour has a reason you could point at in the world.

MP.R01.because: Final Fantasy 10 showed us DO THE ARITHMETIC AND SHOW THE ANSWER. Machine Party shows us WHICH ONE THING TO WITHHOLD. Together they are a rule Bohemia can hold every screen against: the player should know everything about WHAT IS IN THE ROOM and nothing about WHICH ORDER IT COMES IN. A district that tells you it holds four dogs and a man with a pipe, without telling you what is around the next corner, is Valheim-style danger by place done the honest way, and it is the exact opposite of a health bar that hides its own number.
MP.R01.port: TAKE, AND IT IS THE PAIR TO FFX.R01
MP.R01.title: TELL THEM THE COUNT. HIDE ONLY THE ORDER.
MP.R01.what: Buckshot Roulette loads the shotgun in front of you and TELLS YOU EXACTLY how many live rounds and how many blanks are going in. What it never tells you is the ORDER. Two live and three blanks, and no idea which one is next.
MP.R01.why: THIS IS THE BEST INFORMATION DESIGN IN EITHER GAME IN THIS BOOK. Complete information about the composition, zero information about the sequence. Nothing is hidden to create difficulty, so the player never feels cheated, and yet every single pull is a real decision. Hiding the count would make it a coin flip. Showing the order would make it arithmetic. He hides exactly one thing.

MP.R02.because: NO DAMAGE BEFORE THE DIAL is our law, so the numbers wait, but the SHAPE is free and it is a decision the health readout has to make anyway. A countable charge also survives the thumb rule: three big marks read at a glance in the corner of a phone, where a thin bar with a number in it does not.
MP.R02.title: YOUR LIFE IS A COUNT OF CHARGES, NOT A NUMBER
MP.R02.what: Health in Buckshot Roulette is a DEFIBRILLATOR with charges, shown as lightning bolts. Two, three or four. Take a live round to the head and you spend a charge. There is no bar and no percentage.
MP.R02.why: A small countable thing is read instantly and felt physically. Nobody has to translate 62% into "how many more mistakes do I get". Three bolts means three mistakes, and the answer arrives before you have finished looking.

MP.R03.because: Final Fantasy 10 could delete its HUD because it is a corridor (FFX.W03). Klubnika can delete his because the machine is at arm's length in first person. BOHEMIA HAS NEITHER EXCUSE. We are three-quarter view at 44px in an open valley of 27 districts, and he has already reported walking through it lost. Two of the greatest interfaces we have studied both have almost no interface, AND BOTH OF THEM PAID FOR IT WITH SOMETHING WE DO NOT HAVE. That is not a coincidence to admire, it is a bill to notice. We earn a quiet screen with landmarks and light, or we do not get one.
MP.R03.port: REFUSE, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME THIS BOOK HAS SAID THIS
MP.R03.title: THERE IS NO HUD, BECAUSE THE MACHINE IS ALREADY IN FRONT OF YOU
MP.R03.what: Buckshot Roulette is described as "diegetic systems and minimal UI", and s.p.l.i.t goes further: the entire game takes place inside a working terminal, with no HUD elements at all to break the illusion of sitting at the machine.
MP.R03.why: He can delete the HUD because a first-person camera puts a real object at arm's length, and the object carries the information on its own face.

MP.R04.because: Bohemia is a hundred hours and a single character, so it cannot be back to back chaos and should not try. What ports is the AUDIT: every screen between him and the next decision is on trial. Measured already, the run takes 24.2 seconds to first play on throttled 4G and he told us the game "kinda runs like shit". That is the same complaint in his words, and it is a demo blocker.
MP.R04.lens: minimum workload (Hodent) - Pinelle/Wong/Stach, built from what players actually complain about
MP.R04.title: NOTHING WAITS
MP.R04.what: Klubnika's stated design rule for Machine Party: "no fluff, no waiting, just back to back violent chaos." He says they cut down the dialogue, the transitions, and the board-game bits that minigame collections usually carry.
MP.R04.why: The connective tissue is where players quit, and it is invisible to the person who built it because they are proud of it.

MP.W01.because: It is the exact counterweight to FFX.W01, the save point you walk to. Bohemia needs BOTH: a valley where almost nowhere is safe, and a small number of places that are, which you can see from a distance because somebody is keeping the lights on there. Nowhere to rest is what makes a save sphere mean something. Together they are danger by place and light equals territory, already both law.
MP.W01.title: NOWHERE TO REST
MP.W01.what: Brutalism is his named environment inspiration, and the stated reason is behavioural rather than visual: the player never really feels like they can rest anywhere. His work is described as taking after the relentlessness of military organisations.
MP.W01.why: A level rule, not a texture rule. The building refuses you a corner to sit in, and that does more work than any amount of grime.

MP.W02.because: Bohemia has a rack of hundreds of cooked instruments and a 120 BPM law that everything quantises to, so the second channel exists and is further along than the first. But this lane owns ui_deny and the shared rule underneath it: a sound may be the best copy of a message and never the only copy. Klubnika can lean on audio because he is not shipping to a phone on silent in a bright room.
MP.W02.port: ADAPT, AND IT IS THE SOUND LANE'S, NOT MINE
MP.W02.title: THE SOUND IS THE OTHER HALF, NOT A LAYER ON TOP
MP.W02.what: Reviewers of Machine Party keep crediting the audio for the atmosphere, and Alex Peipman's score is called out for a grimy, oppressive consistency that deliberately contrasts with how silly some of the minigames are. Klubnika scores most of his own work.
MP.W02.why: In this family of games the industrial audio is not decoration over the art direction, it is a second channel carrying the same claim.

MP.W03.because: It is already what his 8/27 verdict describes and he may not have noticed he was describing it. THE CUT CORNER is a stamped metal tag, which is Machine Party. THE HEAVY LINE is a thing that was welded rather than drawn, which is Machine Party. GOLD AND COLD is two colours that MEAN two things, you and the machine, which is Final Fantasy 10's discipline exactly. ALL TYPEWRITER WIDTH is a readout on a device, which is both at once. And the dirt died because grime belongs to the room and not to the readout, which is the seam holding. THE LOOK HE PICKED IS ALREADY THE SENTENCE HE SAID, and the next thing built goes on this test: is it readable like Final Fantasy 10, and is it made of something like Machine Party. If it fails either half it is not Bohemia.
MP.W03.port: TAKE. THIS IS THE THESIS OF THE LANE NOW.
MP.W03.title: FINAL FANTASY 10 MEETS MACHINE PARTY, AND THE SEAM IS THE POINT
MP.W03.what: His own words on 8/27, and it is the first time anybody has named what the Bohemia look actually is. Two games at opposite ends of the same book: one is a readable list of numbers laid over a soft tropical world, the other is a filthy steel object with almost no numbers on it at all.
MP.W03.why: They are not opposites, they are two halves of one answer. Final Fantasy 10 is right about INFORMATION: do the arithmetic for the player and show the answer. Machine Party is right about SUBSTANCE: the thing carrying the information should look like it was welded, not designed. What kills most interfaces is having one without the other, either a beautiful object you cannot read or a clean readout with no character in it at all.
